messages:
Ava: Quick sync — we need to lock the runtime 'feature index' API shape. Customer asks rolling in: tool enumeration, streaming support, token limits, and function-calling flags. What do we commit for an MVP?

Ravi: My take: MVP should be small and cacheable. Returnable fields: model_name, model_version, features (list of short feature flags), limits (context and token caps), and tool metadata (name + compatibility tags). Keep it schema-stable.

Sam: Agreed. Also include a 'stability' or 'compat_score' numeric so clients can decide fallbacks. Some customers will want explicit quantization/precision info (fp16/int8). Can be optional.

Priya: Backwards compatibility note: if we extend features later, we should use versioned response (header X-Feature-Index-Version) + feature namespaced keys, not breaking fields. Also add deprecation metadata.

Ava: Good. Prioritization: streaming support is high for real-time chat; tool lists + function-calling detail next; detailed token matrix (per-endpoint) nice-to-have. Thoughts on launch gating?

Ravi: Launch gates I propose: (1) API P95 < 50ms when cached, < 200ms uncached; (2) payload < 5KB typical; (3) integration tests for function-calling metadata with 2 partner customers; (4) rollout behind a flag for 2 weeks.

Sam: Add a quality gate: run 100 sample prompts across three models and ensure reported limits match observed behavior (no silent truncation).

Priya: Customers asking: large retailer needs explicit 'streaming':true and 'streaming_format':"chunks|jsonlines"; fintech wants guaranteed min_context_tokens for audit logs. We should capture both in schema.

Ava: Good call. Keep schema extensible. Also decide whether tools expose an example invocation and output schema in the feature index — that helps SDKs do contract checks.

Ravi: Proposal: tools array with entries: name, id, category, allowed_input_types, example_invocation (optional), and schema_url (optional). Do not inline large schemas — link to hosted small schema blobs.

Sam: Example response sketch (MVP):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-1.2",
  "version": "2026-11-01",
  "features": [
    {"name":"streaming","available":true,"formats":["newline","jsonlines"]},
    {"name":"function_calling","available":true},
    {"name":"tool_calls","available":true}
  ],
  "tools": [
    {"id":"browser_v2","name":"browser","category":"retrieval","allowed_input_types":["url","query"],"example_invocation":"{\"url\": \"https://...\"}","schema_url":"https://internal.s3/schema/browser_v2.json"}
  ],
  "limits": {"context_tokens":65536, "max_input_tokens":32768, "max_output_tokens":32768}
}
```

Priya: That looks good. Keep the top-level 'features' short so clients can gate behavior quickly. Tools can be paginated; include a 'tool_count' and ETag for caching.

Elliot: ops-bot: deploy scheduled: feature-index-v1 -> staging at 2026-11-08T02:00Z. Canary group: 10% internal + 2 partners.

Ava: Launch checklist draft:
- Spec finalized and doced in product repo
- SDKs: small helpers to parse features/tools + fallbacks
- Perf: cached p95 < 50ms, uncached < 200ms
- Security review for schema_url hosting + signed URLs if private
- Acceptance: 2 partner integrations pass tool-call contract tests
- Rollout plan + flag + telemetry (usage, cache hit, errors)

Ravi: For telemetry, emit: feature_index_hit, tool_count, streaming_requested, streaming_supported, mismatch_detected. Also capture feature_index_version in logs.

Sam: Edge cases: partial tool availability (only in Dedicated or Private), model aliases (redwood-1.2 -> redwood-latest), and multi-model bundles. Add 'availability' per tool/feature (hosted/dedicated/private).

Priya: Docs: include migration notes and a short example for SDKs that want to gracefully degrade from streaming -> polling.

Ava: Ok next steps: Ravi, please draft the JSON schema and an example paginated tools response. Sam, add tests for limits/stability. Priya, write an initial rollout/runbook. We'll reconvene Thurs 10am. :thumbsup:
